titleStmt.title: The American Minister (Coleman) to the Latvian Minister for Foreign Affairs (Cielens)

div.head: The American Minister (Coleman) to the Latvian Minister for Foreign Affairs (Cielens)
div.p:
Excellency: Referring to Your Excellency’s note No. 13781, of June 28, 1927, enclosing copies of an English translation of the rules and regulations based on the Latvian admeasurement laws, I now have the honor to inform Your Excellency that the rules set forth in the translation have been compared with those of the United States and the two have been found to be substantially in accord. My Government therefore is prepared to issue the necessary instructions for the recognition of the tonnages set forth in the registers or other national papers of Latvian vessels as measured under the aforesaid rules as the
tonnage of the vessels, so that it will not be necessary for such vessels to be remeasured at any port in the United States.

The issuance of such instructions is conditioned upon a similar recognition being accorded by the Latvian Government to the certificates of registry or other national papers of American ships. Upon receipt of a note from Your Excellency stating that the Latvian Government has issued the necessary instructions for the recognition of the certificates of registry or other national papers of vessels of the United States, together with the date upon which such instructions become effective, my Government will issue appropriate instructions for the recognition of papers of Latvian vessels.

note.p: Note not found in Department files; copies of the rules and regulations were transmitted to the Department in despatch No. 4582, July 1, 1927, from the Minister in Latvia. (File No. 860P.855/3.)
